prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 1997 – Summary (≤500 words)

Vision and approach
- Build a fair, free, open society by widening opportunity, spreading power, and balancing liberty, equality, and community.
- Active, enabling government: invest in people, protect the environment, modernise politics, and tackle inequality.
- Costed programme with clear funding sources (“menu with prices”).

Education (top priority; +£2bn/yr funded by +1p on basic income tax)
- Universal high-quality early years education for all 3–4 year-olds.
- Smaller primary classes (≤30 within 5 years); double spending on books/equipment in year one; £500m over 5 years for repairs.
- Raise standards: General Teaching Council, stronger inspections (including LEAs), discipline/truancy measures, literacy drive, flexible Minimum Curriculum Entitlement (replace National Curriculum).
- Oppose selection; bring GM schools/CTCs into a “light-touch” LEA framework; phase out Assisted Places and foster state–independent partnerships.
- Lifelong learning: Individual Learning Accounts; fair, income-linked student repayments; oppose top-up fees; credit-based post-14 system; 2% remissible training levy (SMEs exempt).

Economy, jobs, enterprise
- Stability: independent Reserve Bank (BoE) to target low inflation; “golden rule” on borrowing; distinguish capital vs current spend; public–private investment.
- Get people back to work: convert benefits to “working benefits”; invest in skills (education spend) and infrastructure; shift tax from jobs to pollution; promote saving (new SAYE-style schemes).
- SMEs: tackle late payment (statutory interest), expand finance, cut red tape, long-term replace UBR; regional Development Agencies; boost civil R&D and tech transfer.
- Competition/consumers/utilities: stronger competition law; single Office of Utility Regulation; tougher consumer rights and financial regulation; clear GM food labelling.

Environment, energy, transport
- Green tax shift (incl. gradual carbon tax) to cut CO2 by 30% from 1990 in 15 years and reduce taxes on jobs/VAT; new environmental indicators; stronger Environment Agency; separate environment/energy department.
- Public transport first: enable urban road pricing to fund clean transit; London Underground public, private finance for investment; treble rail freight and double passengers by 2010, enforceable targets on Railtrack.
- Motoring: reduce annual car tax to £10 for ≤1600cc, funded by ~4p/litre fuel duty rise; reform company car tax.
- National home insulation programme to end fuel poverty; efficiency standards; back renewables; no subsidies for new nuclear; focus nuclear on decommissioning/waste.

Safety, housing, communities
- 3,000 more police on the beat; faster, more effective justice; restorative youth justice; Royal Commission on drugs; stronger victim support; tackle hate crime.
- Housing: build more through public–private–housing association partnerships; release council capital receipts; new Mortgage Benefit for first-time buyers (retain MIRAS for existing loans); end rough sleeping by 2000; tenant rights; bring empty homes into use.
- Rural/urban: reform CAP to countryside contracts; protect fisheries via regional management; improve rural services/transport; urban regeneration, coordinated transport, “planning for real.”

NHS and health
- Maintain free, comprehensive NHS funded by taxation; +£540m+/yr (close NIC loopholes + 5p/pack cigarettes).
- Six-month halt on finance-driven closures; independent audit; recruit more frontline staff (+£200m/yr); max 6-month waits within 3 years.
- End two-tier GP fundholding; National Inspectorate for Health & Social Care; restore free eye/dental checks; shift to prevention; independent Food Commission.

Welfare, opportunity, equality
- Break poverty traps: raise tax thresholds (+£200; ~500k out of tax); new 50% rate on £100k+; simplify benefits into Low Income Benefit; childcare strategy; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally variable minimum wage; crack down on fraud/evasion.
- Older people: earnings-linked top-up for poorest pensioners; flexible retirement 60–70; anti–age discrimination; replace SERPS with secure personal/occupational pensions (accrued rights protected).
- Rights and inclusion: Bill of Rights (ECHR in UK law); Freedom of Information; cut quangos; referendums on constitutional change.
- Political reform: PR for all elections; reduce MPs by ~200; predominantly elected second chamber; fixed 4-year terms.
- Devolution: Home Rule for Scotland and Wales (PR, tax-varying); English regional assemblies where demanded; London strategic authority; strengthen/localise council finance (long-term Local Income Tax).
- Equality: women’s workplace/pension/NHS fairness; civil rights for disabled; action on racism; non-discriminatory immigration/asylum; LGBT equality incl. equal age of consent and repeal Section 28.

Europe, defence, global role
- Pro-European reform and enlargement; PR for MEPs (by 1999); more majority voting with key vetoes retained; join single currency if criteria met and referendum approves.
- Strong defence via NATO; retain Trident at reduced warheads; UN reform (peacekeeping, ICC); lead on climate treaties; increase aid towards 0.7% GNP in 10 years; debt relief; strict arms controls and landmine ban; fair trade with labour/environment standards.

Tax pledges
- Transparent, costed changes; 1p on basic rate for education; +5p on cigarettes for health checks; fairer distribution with most adults paying lower or unchanged income tax and average taxpayers facing minimal net changes.
